title: Bound a long-running step
summary: A timeout stops waiting after a chosen limit. It keeps stuck work from occupying an agent indefinitely.
introduction: A timeout stops waiting after a chosen limit. It keeps stuck work from occupying an agent indefinitely. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A timeout stops waiting after a chosen limit. It keeps stuck work from occupying an agent indefinitely.

blocks.title: Bound a long-running step

blocks.text: The wrapped work has a two-minute limit. This tiny echo finishes much sooner.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose a reasonable limit for a local unit-test step.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A timeout is a limit, not evidence that the work is correct.
For more detail later, use this [Jenkins further reading](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/).

seo.title: Jenkins: Bound a long-running step
